tests.survivingOwner: packages/ui/src/components/workflows/steps/steps-logic.test.ts: a block with no outputs (Stop) never splices: it becomes another branch

tests.name: inserts a block into an edge: source → new → target
tests.reason: Duplicate addBlock edge insertion is exercised by the named Steps action through the same production owner; its complete literal edge-set assertions are stronger than this subset check. Fails unique-protection bar 6.
tests.survivingOwner: packages/ui/src/components/workflows/steps/steps-logic.test.ts: splices into a chain without losing downstream connections

tests.name: removes blocks with their edges and pinned outputs
tests.reason: Removing a block must also remove incident edges and its pinned output; Steps healing tests do not protect pinned-state cleanup.

tests.name: start → tap a block: connects, back to idle
tests.reason: Two taps must produce the exact requested connection and leave picking mode; no rendering or private React props are inspected.

tests.name: a refused target keeps picking and says why
tests.reason: Rejected target must leave picking active with explanation and permit a later valid target; validator-only tests do not protect the interaction state.

tests.name: its own block or Cancel ends it; a tap while idle does nothing; a new start replaces
tests.reason: Self-tap/cancel must clear pending connection, idle tap does nothing and new source replaces old selection; prevents accidental stale-source edges.

tests.name: a character replaces the selection; the caret goes after it
tests.reason: Symbol insertion/replacement must preserve surrounding text for forward/backward selections and place the caret after inserted content.

tests.name: {{ }} puts the caret inside, or wraps the selection
tests.reason: Expression shortcut must produce syntactically usable braces around a selected expression or position the caret inside an empty expression.

tests.name: Tab indents by the editor's unit
tests.reason: Tab must use the caller-selected indentation and move the caret consistently; actual edit result, not key declaration inventory.

tests.name: drops colours, cursor moves, OSC titles and links
tests.reason: ANSI colors/cursor/OSC sequences and unsafe control bytes must not leak into displayed text, while legitimate text and tabs remain.

tests.name: carries an escape sequence split across chunks
tests.reason: Escape sequences split between chunks must be consumed without losing ordinary text; single-chunk sanitizer coverage cannot catch carry mistakes.

tests.name: keeps what a terminal would show
tests.reason: Carriage-return progress must replace its prior line and CRLF must terminate once; ordinary newline splitting does not protect terminal-style output.

tests.name: splits chunks into lines and keeps the line in progress
tests.reason: Chunk boundaries must preserve incomplete lines without duplicating/dropping content; literal words form an independent stream oracle.

tests.name: reads a finished log to its end, window after window, by the daemon's offsets
tests.reason: Finished logs must read all server windows using raw-byte cursors even when redaction expands displayed text; otherwise portions duplicate/vanish.

tests.name: polls a live log, and a failed read resumes from the same offset once — no duplicates
tests.reason: A transient live-read failure must retry the same offset and continue without duplicate text, then cease polling at terminal EOF.

tests.name: an error on a finished log is reported, not appended
tests.reason: A failed completed-log read must report an error without adding error text as log content; live retries exercise a different branch.

tests.name: stop() ends it: no further reads, including after wake
tests.reason: Stopping the viewer must terminate polling and make later wake inert, avoiding background log requests after unmount.

tests.name: a live log held at a partial last line waits for the next poll instead of spinning
tests.reason: A held partial line with no cursor advance must wait for a poll rather than spin synchronous reads; the transport stub supplies the documented stalled cursor, not retry logic.

tests.name: readWholeLog reads every window to the end (the download)
tests.reason: Full download must concatenate every log window rather than only the displayed tail or first response; follower and download are separate implementations.

tests.name: parseWorkflowLogWindow reads the X-Log-* headers, case-insensitively
tests.reason: Case-insensitive X-Log headers must decode cursor/eof/size/live correctly and missing headers fall back to raw response bytes; concrete wire protocol parser.

tests.name: splices into a chain without losing downstream connections
tests.reason: Adding after an occupied output must preserve downstream chain connections; this selection/splice decision is distinct from lower canvas insertion mutation. Surviving owner also asserts the requested new block type, preserving the unique type assertion from removed direct canvas setup without another execution.

tests.name: a block with no outputs (Stop) never splices: it becomes another branch
tests.reason: Adding Stop must keep existing downstream path as a sibling branch because Stop has no onward output; prevents silently cutting off workflow work. Surviving owner also asserts the requested new block type, preserving the unique type assertion from removed direct canvas setup without another execution.

tests.name: the first step goes after the trigger; with no trigger, loose
tests.reason: The first executable step must attach to an available trigger, while a new trigger in an empty graph remains standalone.

tests.name: connect candidates: connectable first, with why the rest cannot
tests.reason: Connect choices must omit self/triggers and favor legal targets while explaining illegal ancestors; edge validation alone cannot detect missing legal choices.

tests.name: move to another output: re-hangs the row's edge; loops are refused
tests.reason: Moving must change the selected incoming edge and preserve downstream edges; refused descendant move must keep graph intact and current candidate identified.

tests.name: deleting a middle step heals the chain
tests.reason: Deleting a simple middle step must heal predecessor→successor rather than cut off downstream work.

tests.name: a join (two edges in) is deleted without guessing a heal
tests.reason: Deleting a multi-input join must avoid inventing ambiguous replacement paths, preserving independent upstream branches.

tests.name: duplicate puts the copy right after the original, taking over what it fed
tests.reason: Duplicate-after must splice the copied block into the selected chain; clipboard reminting tests do not own Steps graph wiring.

tests.name: disable / enable
tests.reason: Disable/enable must affect only the selected block IDs and reverse cleanly; false-versus-omitted property spelling is not asserted.

tests.name: Back closes the overlay; a refused close holds a fresh entry; a UI close gives it back
tests.reason: Browser Back must ask the mounted phone overlay to close, rearm after refusal and release its history entry after a UI close. Detects navigation leaving the app or calling close twice; the pure history-stack tests do not exercise hook registration and React state.

tests.name: a resting finger opens it once, where it rests, and the click that follows is swallowed
tests.reason: A completed touch press opens once at the input point, suppresses its synthetic click and permits a subsequent ordinary tap. Detects duplicate actions or a menu opening at the wrong pointer data. Replace imported timeout-derived assertions with fake-timer completion/cancellation; retain a literal short-tap check and remove the otherwise unused exported timeout.

tests.name: a tap stays a click
tests.reason: A short touch ending after 200 virtual ms must stay a click and leave no delayed menu action. Detects immediate press classification or failure to cancel its timer. Replace imported timeout-derived assertions with fake-timer completion/cancellation; retain a literal short-tap check and remove the otherwise unused exported timeout.

tests.name: a finger that moves (or that the browser takes for a scroll) is not a press
tests.reason: A moved or browser-cancelled touch must never open its menu after pending timers drain. Detects scrolling opening a context menu. Replace imported timeout-derived assertions with fake-timer completion/cancellation; retain a literal short-tap check and remove the otherwise unused exported timeout.

tests.name: a mouse never starts the timer; its right click opens the menu
tests.reason: Mouse pointer-down must not become a touch press; right-click must open the menu and suppress the native context menu. Detects wrong input-device classification. Replace imported timeout-derived assertions with fake-timer completion/cancellation; retain a literal short-tap check and remove the otherwise unused exported timeout.

tests.name: Android's long-press contextmenu and the timer open it once between them
tests.reason: Android contextmenu-before-timer and timer-before-contextmenu must each open exactly once and suppress the following click. Detects duplicate menus across the two event orderings. Replace imported timeout-derived assertions with fake-timer completion/cancellation; retain a literal short-tap check and remove the otherwise unused exported timeout.

tests.name: a mouse event the touch still emits does not reach the menu's outside-click listener
tests.reason: The synthetic mouse-down following a completed touch must not reach an outside-click handler, while a fresh mouse-down must. Detects a newly opened menu immediately closing itself. Replace imported timeout-derived assertions with fake-timer completion/cancellation; retain a literal short-tap check and remove the otherwise unused exported timeout.

tests.name: a row unmounted mid-press opens nothing
tests.reason: Unmounting a row with a pending press must cancel it. Detects a detached row opening a menu after navigation. Replace imported timeout-derived assertions with fake-timer completion/cancellation; retain a literal short-tap check and remove the otherwise unused exported timeout.

tests.name: an id naming an Object.prototype member falls back to the generic icon instead of crashing
tests.reason: Wire-supplied registry ids matching Object.prototype keys must render a nonempty fallback rather than resolve inherited methods as React components. Detects a reproducible crash from ids such as constructor; no other rendering test uses these ids.

tests.name: reads no list as every account, the System login last when included
tests.reason: No allow-list means all managed accounts; opt-in system login follows them. Detects hiding available accounts or silently choosing system credentials.

tests.name: matches ids, then labels, keeps list order, and reports entries naming nobody
tests.reason: Detects resolving an account label to the wrong credential, changing fixed priority, losing missing-account warnings, or duplicating selected identities.

tests.name: unticks an account into a list, and back to no list when all are ticked
tests.reason: Checkbox edits must encode the intended allowed credential set in AccountPolicy; detects accidental all-account permission after an exclusion.

tests.name: never writes an empty list (the engine would read it as every account)
tests.reason: Unchecking the last account must refuse an empty allow-list because daemon semantics interpret it as every credential, a concrete privilege widening bug.

tests.name: excludes accounts in fixed order, keeping the order of the rest
tests.reason: Removing and restoring credentials must preserve the remaining fixed priority; otherwise the next run uses the wrong account.

tests.name: moves accounts in fixed order and drops a list that is back in the family's order
tests.reason: Reordering must change account priority and respect endpoints/system identity without changing allowed membership; adjacent toggle tests do not exercise movement.

tests.name: adds and removes the System login in a list
tests.reason: System opt-in/out must update both wire flags and explicit membership; otherwise the daemon may run under unintended host credentials.

tests.name: keeps entries naming nobody until they are dropped
tests.reason: An unrelated checkbox edit must preserve unknown account references; explicit removal and allow-all actions have separately specified data effects.

tests.name: drops an order-only list when leaving fixed order, and keeps a real restriction
tests.reason: Strategy changes must preserve credential restrictions while removing ordering that no longer applies; detects silently broadening a restricted policy.

tests.name: lists reported windows, each rule for them, then rules for windows not reported
tests.reason: Every configured scoped quota rule must remain editable, including missing and case-equivalent reported windows; literal rule indices identify the persisted policy entry, not visual geometry.

tests.name: the same message on another channel does not reach workflows
tests.reason: An unrelated event channel could mutate workflow state; the positive route test prevents a reject-all implementation from passing.

tests.name: opens one tab per workflow per project, reusing it and updating its run
tests.reason: Opening/reopening a workflow must preserve one tab per project, selection and omitted-versus-null run identity; other tab cases do not exercise reuse.

tests.name: an unknown workflow takes the caller's title
tests.reason: Before list loading completes a newly opened tab must use the caller-supplied name, not lose it.

tests.name: follows a rename and closes with its workflow, handing the focus on
tests.reason: Remote rename/delete must update every project tab and transfer focus after removal; reducer tests cannot detect stale app tab state.

tests.name: closeTab closes a workflow tab like any local tab
tests.reason: Explicit closeTab must remove the workflow tab and active selection; remote-delete coverage uses another action.

tests.name: resolves each entry against its own agent's loaded catalogue and keeps the rest
tests.reason: New requests must name live slugs per provider without changing unrelated account policy or unknown providers; catches cross-provider model selection and stale aliases.

tests.name: never resolves against a list that may be a fallback: pending, degraded or errored
tests.reason: Unready provider fallback catalogues must not overwrite stored live slugs; literal status fixtures differ from live resolution and catch data loss during discovery.

tests.name: a fresh agent block names a listed model; other blocks are their defaults
tests.reason: Fresh blocks resolve against provider defaults independently of complete template requests; catches creation of a block with an immediately invalid model.

tests.name: carries the selected blocks and only the edges between them, under the marker
tests.reason: Only selected nodes and internal edges travel with literal interoperable marker bytes; paste tests do not prove exported payload boundaries.

tests.name: is not fooled by other text, or by a payload whose blocks do not parse
tests.reason: Unrelated text, unsupported marker versions and malformed node payloads must not paste; the unsupported-version fixture otherwise contains a valid node.

tests.name: re-mints ids and names and keeps inner edges and references
tests.reason: Paste must remint identity and internal references while retaining external references; a sequential/string-only rename would corrupt continued sessions or templates.

tests.name: keeps a name that is free in the target workflow (a paste across workflows)
tests.reason: Cross-workflow paste must preserve an unoccupied name; collision tests exercise a distinct branch.

tests.name: does not turn A→B, B→C renames into A→C
tests.reason: Simultaneous Post/Post2 collisions must not cascade into references to the wrong copied node; literals independently identify the intended destinations.

tests.name: parses ?workflow=&run=
tests.reason: URL workflow/run identifiers must parse and unsafe/invalid identifiers reject; message parsing has a separate input format.

tests.name: strips its parameters and keeps the rest
tests.reason: Consuming a link must remove only workflow/run query fields and preserve other query/hash/path state, avoiding repeated opens or lost routes.

tests.name: parses the service worker's message; anything else is null
tests.reason: Only the literal service-worker message type with valid identity may navigate; URL parsing cannot detect malformed bridge messages.

tests.name: one pending link, taken once, listeners told
tests.reason: Newest pending notification navigation must be delivered once rather than replay old/opened targets; subscriber/queue seam is used by WorkflowsHost.

tests.name: waits for the connection and the workflows, opens in the workflow's own project
tests.reason: Navigation must wait for a connection/loading, choose the workflow project and distinguish a removed workflow; URL decoding does not own readiness.

tests.name: converts typed values to the canonical unit without float noise
tests.reason: Typed fractional hours/minutes must become mathematically correct persisted minutes/seconds; literal 30/6/20/90 values catch unit or floating-point conversion errors.

tests.name: clamps in the canonical unit, never at a converted bound
tests.reason: A one-minute minimum must remain exactly one minute after hour editing; detects rounding the converted floor into an invalid stored bound.

tests.name: a missing workflow is an error with words, not a crash
tests.reason: A missing remote workflow must yield an error state and no editable draft, not throw through the editor.

tests.name: saves 600 ms after the last change, once, with the revision the draft is based on
tests.reason: Edits must debounce 600ms from the last edit and submit the latest draft against its known revision; literal time comes from §7.2, not imported production constants.

tests.name: serializes saves: a change during a save is saved right after it, on the new revision
tests.reason: A save crossing another edit must not issue concurrent stale writes or discard the newer edit; held network response exposes a real revision race.

tests.name: a failed save says so and keeps the edit; flush retries it
tests.reason: A transport failure must retain unsaved user text and flush must retry it; the fake provides failure/success responses, not editor state logic.

tests.name: an enabled draft the daemon refuses as invalid is saved disabled, and the editor says so
tests.reason: An invalid enabled draft must retain the edit by saving it disabled and expose that state to the user, per errors-block-enabling-not-saving requirement.

tests.name: a 409 raises the banner and stops autosaving
tests.reason: A stale revision response must stop automatic overwrite attempts and expose conflict; otherwise another client's edit is silently lost.

tests.name: Reload takes their copy and drops the edits (and the undo history)
tests.reason: Reload must take the remote version and clear stale local history; the conflict prompt's discard action differs from overwrite.

tests.name: Keep mine overwrites theirs with the draft
tests.reason: Keep mine must fetch current revision and save the retained draft; otherwise a conflict cannot be resolved in favor of local edits.

tests.name: a newer revision while clean reloads silently
tests.reason: A newer remote revision must refresh a clean editor; dirty-draft conflict coverage cannot detect stale clean views.

tests.name: a newer revision over unsaved edits raises the banner
tests.reason: A remote update must preserve unsaved local edits and surface conflict; save-response 409 coverage does not exercise the event path.

tests.name: an own-save event before its response preserves the draft without a false conflict
tests.reason: An own-save event can precede its HTTP answer without generating a false conflict or losing edits; distinct event/response race.

tests.name: undo drops a selection of blocks the older draft does not have
tests.reason: Undoing an inserted node must drop its selected identity, preventing an inspector selection pointing at a nonexistent node; history-only snapshots cannot prove this.

tests.name: enabling saves pending edits first, then patches set_enabled on the new revision
tests.reason: Enable must flush pending draft first and patch the new revision; otherwise enabling creates stale conflicts or loses the latest edit.

tests.name: validates the draft a moment after each change
tests.reason: Editing an expression to reference a missing node must publish validation problems; validator tests do not prove validation is scheduled after a UI edit.

tests.name: a block naming a profile the loaded list does not hold is flagged as the daemon flags it; none is checked before the list loads
tests.reason: Profile validation must wait for a loaded profile list, warn for a missing id and clear the warning when the profile arrives. Detects false validation errors during loading or a permanently stale profile warning.

tests.name: marks a model the live catalogue does not list, as the daemon does — and follows the catalogue
tests.reason: Remove exact model diagnostic prose; keep error severity, node identity, field path and eventual disappearance after catalogue refresh. These stable data identify the invalid choice.

tests.name: a catalogue not loaded yet raises no false errors
tests.reason: Partial registry/provider discovery must not block valid edits with invented unknown-model errors; distinguishes not-loaded warnings from invalid live models.

tests.name: a reconnect's new client keeps the same editor and its unsaved draft (keyed by connection id)
tests.reason: A rebuilt client for the same connection must retain unsaved draft and write through the new transport, while another connection gets isolated state.

tests.name: a load that lands after the user typed keeps the edit and raises the banner
tests.reason: Typing while a remote load is pending must not let its answer replace newer user text; held GET response demonstrates the race.

tests.name: an Enable event before its response preserves enabled state without a false conflict
tests.reason: An enable event preceding its HTTP answer must not falsely conflict or revert enabled state; separate patch path from save echoes.

tests.name: undo never flips enabled
tests.reason: Undo must restore edited content while leaving enabled state alone; undoing rename must not accidentally resume/pause triggers.

tests.name: reconnect: a failed save is retried; a newer daemon revision is a conflict
tests.reason: Reconnect must retry a failed dirty save only when the daemon revision still matches, otherwise preserve the draft as conflict.

tests.name: flushAllWorkflowEditors saves a pending edit at once (pagehide)
tests.reason: The pagehide flush operation must submit a pending draft before the debounce fires; editor registry iteration is production lifecycle ownership.

tests.name: drops the other kind's fields and keeps unknown ones
tests.reason: Switching Wait variants must remove incompatible fields and retain forward-compatible data; same-kind re-selection must not reset an existing wait.

tests.name: times a run: its duration once ended, the time so far while running
tests.reason: Live duration uses elapsed time and ended duration uses recorded duration, with unknown start remaining unknown; these are displayed numeric data rather than prose.

tests.name: shows the running run over a queued one
tests.reason: When queued and running runs coexist, the card must report the running one; run-mode selection owns a different run list and policy.

tests.name: filters by scope, by running, and by the search
tests.reason: Project/running/search filters must expose the right workflow IDs and normalize trailing slashes; a failed filter hides the user's workflows.

tests.name: a blank workflow is one manual trigger the daemon names and places, in the browser's time zone
tests.reason: Blank-create request must carry a manual trigger, selected project and timezone without invented node IDs; this is caller-visible REST data rather than a template markup snapshot.

tests.name: defaults to this project, and resolves each target
tests.reason: New-workflow form must resolve this/other/temp clone choices to their correct target paths and trimmed input; daemon schema does not own form-to-request conversion.

tests.name: names the first thing missing
tests.reason: Incomplete/oversized creation data must report the missing field and refuse submission; successful resolution cases supply the complementary positive control.

tests.name: maps each trigger whose last poll failed to its error, and nothing else
tests.reason: Poll failure messages must be associated with the correct trigger ID and absent failures omitted; backend trigger tests cannot prove UI association.

tests.name: undo hands back the state before each change, redo walks forward again
tests.reason: Undo/redo must return chronological pre-edit snapshots and stop at the ends; editor integration cases do not cover multi-step replay.

tests.name: a burst with one key is one step; a pause or another key starts a new one
tests.reason: A drag/typing burst must undo in one step while a pause or different field starts another; prevents fragmented or conflated user undo operations.

tests.name: null keys and history navigation keep separate edit steps
tests.reason: Explicit non-coalesced edits and edits following undo/redo must remain separate history steps. Detects a user undo skipping edits because history navigation accidentally continued the previous burst.

tests.name: a new change after an undo drops what could be redone
tests.reason: Editing after undo must discard the abandoned redo branch, preventing restoration of superseded user work.

tests.name: keeps at most 100 steps, dropping the oldest
tests.reason: History must enforce the independently specified 100-step retention without discarding newer edits first; no geometry assertion.

tests.name: offers the roots right after {{
tests.reason: An opening expression must offer valid language roots and prefix filtering; roots are independently documented expression names, not UI copy.

tests.name: walks nodes → a block → output → its known fields, from the caret back
tests.reason: Nested node/output/error/PR paths must suggest accessible properties and replace only the typed suffix; this catches invalid completions or overwriting surrounding text.

tests.name: knows the trigger's fields, the run, the project, the secrets and the input
tests.reason: Context-specific trigger/run/project/secret/input completions must expose values supported by the expression protocol; dynamic secret names are supplied data.

tests.name: offers filters after a pipe, with arguments filled in
tests.reason: Pipe completion must yield executable filter syntax including required arguments; path completion tests cannot detect malformed filter insertion.

tests.name: says nothing outside an expression, after one closed, or after an escape
tests.reason: Plain, closed or escaped expression text must not activate completion; otherwise editor typing is interrupted outside the template language.

tests.name: offers {variables} in a prompt only, and never inside {{
tests.reason: Saved-prompt single-brace variables are enabled only in prompt scope; ordinary template fields must not receive unsupported expansions.

tests.name: refuses JSON over the pinned-data limit
tests.reason: Pinned-data form must reject payloads above the independent 1 MiB storage limit before saving them.

tests.name: refuses null, which set_pinned would read as unpin
tests.reason: Reject null to avoid removing a pin; preserve false and zero as real JSON values. These independent protocol sentinels catch truthiness bugs.

tests.name: explains a syntax error
tests.reason: Malformed JSON must return an actionable error instead of throwing through the form or accepting broken data; valid scalar case supplies a positive control.

tests.name: writes the template reference to a block's output
tests.reason: Copied template text must use the literal documented nodes.Name.output grammar; these are executable bytes, not optional presentation wording.

tests.name: pins a whole recorded output as is, without asking the daemon
tests.reason: A whole recorded output must be pinnable without an unnecessary request. Detects replacing valid recorded data or requiring a network round trip before pinning.

tests.name: reads the whole output when the run kept only a preview
tests.reason: A truncated recorded output must be replaced by the full daemon output before pinning. Detects a subsequent test run executing against preview data.

tests.name: refuses a malformed answer rather than pinning the preview
tests.reason: A malformed full-output response must reject instead of pinning preview data. Detects silent corruption of pinned test-run inputs after a bad response.

tests.name: joins managed accounts to their windows by id; an expired window says nothing
tests.reason: Managed-account usage must join by account identity, omit wrong families and treat expired/stale readings as unknown; selecting another account's usage changes allow-list decisions.

tests.name: loads persisted choices field by field and falls back on unreadable data
tests.reason: Malformed localStorage fields cannot poison UI state or discard independently valid fields; literal versioned storage key is the persistence contract.

tests.name: escapes quoted keys and keeps root paths usable
tests.reason: Copyable expression paths must escape quotes and remain syntactically valid at object/array roots; literal paths catch corrupt template references.

tests.name: pages children with their paths
tests.reason: Pages must include the requested array segment/object values with valid paths and no children for leaves; wrong page offsets lose displayed/copied data, not merely row geometry.

tests.name: copies strings raw and preserves JSON values
tests.reason: Copying strings must preserve raw text while objects preserve JSON structure; double-quoting strings or corrupting nested JSON breaks user clipboard data.

tests.name: reads notify settings field-wise, defaulting to failures only
tests.reason: Missing/malformed notify settings must safely default failures on/successes off while honoring valid booleans; store-success examples do not cover malformed field fallback.

tests.name: counts a Stop block's end as a success and a cancel or a skip as nothing
tests.reason: Observe finishedRunNotice output for terminal statuses under failure-only or success-only preferences, and quiet statuses with both enabled; remove direct internal classification assertions and runOutcomeKind export. Catch missing/spurious actual notices rather than private enum labels.

tests.name: preserves the failure's error, project and test-run identity in its toast
tests.reason: Move unique failure data/project/test metadata and default-success suppression assertions into the existing finished-event→notification-store scenario, then remove duplicate direct helper execution.
tests.survivingOwner: packages/ui/src/lib/workflows/notifications.test.ts: raises a toast and an entry once per run, however often the event arrives

tests.name: says nothing about a sub-workflow's run
tests.reason: Move unique sub-workflow suppression assertions into the existing finished-event→notification-store scenario, then remove duplicate direct helper execution.
tests.survivingOwner: packages/ui/src/lib/workflows/notifications.test.ts: raises a toast and an entry once per run, however often the event arrives

tests.name: puts failed runs in the Attention Center, never test runs
tests.reason: Move unique attention navigation/error payload and test-run exclusion assertions into the existing finished-event→notification-store scenario, then remove duplicate direct helper execution.
tests.survivingOwner: packages/ui/src/lib/workflows/notifications.test.ts: raises a toast and an entry once per run, however often the event arrives

tests.name: raises a toast and an entry once per run, however often the event arrives
tests.reason: Surviving event→store owner now verifies deduplication plus failure data, attention navigation fields, child-run exclusion, default-success suppression and test-run metadata/attention exclusion. It exercises the same public helper algorithms together with actual event sanitization and state publication.

tests.name: stays quiet for the run the user is looking at
tests.reason: A visible run already being viewed must not notify; mounted state is distinct from explicitly marking an ended run read.

tests.name: a mounted run in a hidden document does not swallow the failure
tests.reason: A hidden document must still surface its mounted run's failure; otherwise background completion silently disappears.

tests.name: viewing a LIVE run never silences its later failure
tests.reason: Merely viewing a still-live run must not silence its later failure after leaving; prevents premature read acknowledgement.

tests.name: the workflow summary's notify settings decide (a success toast when asked, no failure when off)
tests.reason: Current workflow summary preferences must control failure suppression/success notification; direct pure-rule tests do not exercise preference lookup.

tests.name: clears a run's toast and entry once it is viewed, and stays quiet about it after
tests.reason: Viewing one ended run clears only its notices and suppresses replay, while other runs remain visible; distinguishes read state from global dismissal.

tests.name: dismisses the toasts and one entry at a time
tests.reason: Dismiss-all toast and dismiss-one attention commands must not accidentally clear unrelated entries or attention state.

tests.name: reads the workflow's notify settings from a loaded run's definition
tests.reason: Without a summary, the loaded frozen definition must supply notification preferences, and successful runs never become failure attention entries.

tests.name: forgets everything on a connection switch
tests.reason: Reset must clear notices and deduplication memory so the same ID on another connection can notify; it tests the public reset operation, not connection-switch wiring.

tests.name: every listener takes the run, and unsubscribing takes it out
tests.reason: Open-run delivery must reach subscribers, stop after unsubscribe, and report no listeners so navigation fallback can work.

tests.name: only a chat tab with a whole workflow owner links to a run
tests.reason: Only complete workflow-owned agent-chat identity may link to a run; malformed/foreign/shell owner data must not navigate to an unusable target.

tests.name: per block: status, duration (live for a running one), attempt, handle, account and hops
tests.reason: Overlay must preserve actual block duration, selected account, attempt, activity and handle while omitting unreached blocks; independent from timeline mapping owner.

tests.name: edges: taken, active into a running block, dead, idle — read off the source when the lists lag
tests.reason: Edges must distinguish executed/live-target/dead/unreached paths even before recorded edge lists catch up; wrong colors here convey wrong execution data, not geometry.

tests.name: a failed block takes its error edge unless the run records another path
tests.reason: Failed blocks use error edges and explicit recorded paths override inferred handles; prevents falsely reporting success routes after failure.

tests.name: leaves the config untouched when the kind is already chosen
tests.reason: Re-picking HTTP body kind must not destroy form fields or text content type already entered by the user.

tests.name: carries a written value across, and starts JSON as an empty object
tests.reason: HTTP body edits must preserve entered text when convertible, clear removed bodies and create valid JSON for a newly enabled body.

tests.name: keeps the success statuses when their mode is re-picked, and restores the latest list
tests.reason: Switching response acceptance mode must not discard the remembered custom status codes; parser tests do not own form state conversion.

tests.name: reads codes separated by commas, semicolons or spaces, once each, in order
tests.reason: User-entered HTTP status lists must preserve numeric meanings and remove duplicate codes across supported separators.

tests.name: names what isn't a status code
tests.reason: HTTP codes outside 100..599 and nonnumeric tokens must surface validation problems; a positive valid list prevents reject-all behavior.

tests.name: accepts JSON, with expressions standing in for values or inside strings
tests.reason: Valid HTTP JSON templates containing raw expression values or quoted strings must not be blocked by JSON-only parsing.

tests.name: accepts exactly one expression: its value is encoded as JSON
tests.reason: An entire HTTP JSON body may be a raw expression; prefix/suffix whitespace cannot make that protocol form invalid.

tests.name: names a body that won't parse, without positions into the stand-in text
tests.reason: Invalid JSON structure must show a problem without offsets into generated placeholder text; fixtures include adjacent expressions and unquoted keys.

tests.name: plans one row per distinct expression
tests.reason: Repeated references to the same shell expression must share one environment row while different expressions receive distinct usable variables. Detects duplicate mappings or one expression overwriting another.

tests.name: never suggests a name the shell, the loader or a common tool reads
tests.reason: Use literal dangerous shell/tool names as an independent forbidden set and assert proposed names are usable, nonreserved and carry the expression. Remove exact WF_ naming and circular isReservedEnvName oracle; make that helper internal.

tests.name: never takes a name a row or a word of the script already uses
tests.reason: Keep collisions with existing environment and script assignments plus invalid-name avoidance; assert names are distinct from occupied names, not arbitrary numeric suffix selection.

tests.name: reuses a row only when it holds exactly that expression and wins at run time
tests.reason: Keep exact-match reuse and rejection of whitespace/prefix/filter/shadowed/reserved mismatches, asserting reused versus newly allocated identity without freezing invented new names.

tests.name: doesn't reuse a row the script itself sets or reads other than as $NAME
tests.reason: Keep assignment/read/nameref/default-assignment collision cases and plain-read reuse, with independent A identity instead of prescribed INPUT_A fallback.

tests.name: keeps every row as it was, fields a newer version wrote included
tests.reason: Keep unknown fields and reused existing rows, then assert the appended expression value; remove new variable spelling irrelevant to persisted-data preservation.

tests.name: adds nothing the second time, also once the script reads the variables
tests.reason: Keep idempotence and halfway-manual-replacement reuse; build the second input from actual suggested identities, with unchanged environment as the independent idempotence oracle.

tests.name: leaves Go-style {{.Field}} alone and notes a broken expression
tests.reason: Keep expression/Go-template discrimination and incomplete-state output; remove invented INPUT_REPO spelling.

tests.name: flags environment names the shell block fails on, and repeats
tests.reason: Environment row editing must identify invalid names, missing names and shadowed duplicates; last-row-wins semantics comes from shell environment execution.

tests.name: flags header names the HTTP block fails on and nameless rows it skips
tests.reason: Invalid HTTP header tokens must error while query names may contain spaces; missing name with data must warn rather than silently lose input.

tests.name: moves the value as the daemon applies it, capped at the type's maximum
tests.reason: Migration of legacy timeout values must preserve minutes for processes, convert to seconds for HTTP and honor independent 24h/1h limits.

tests.name: has nothing to move for other types or without a value
tests.reason: Migration must not invent a process timeout for agent blocks or absent legacy values; positive migration cases prevent no-op implementations passing.

tests.name: preserves failed block details and distinguishes unreached steps in a finished run
tests.reason: Completed runs must retain errors/attempt/duration and mark unreached blocks skipped; failed block must be selected for diagnosis.

tests.name: shows a working agent's account, hops and activity
tests.reason: Live agent steps must show the current account/activity/duration and select that step while downstream unstarted steps remain pending; finished-run case cannot detect premature skipped state.

tests.name: builds a block's input from its live upstreams
tests.reason: Run details must reconstruct trigger/single live branch inputs and exclude untaken/skipped edges; inspector DataTab uses a distinct implementation.

tests.name: merges several live inputs by name
tests.reason: Multiple live inputs merge under predecessor names and propagate truncation; single-source case does not catch overwrite or false-whole display.

tests.name: offers what makes sense now
tests.reason: Only meaningful cancel/retry/retry-failed/delete-temp actions are offered for current run state; wrong actions affect caller-visible commands.

tests.name: retries with the same input, or from the same event
tests.reason: Retries must preserve input/event/test identity and avoid empty requests before trigger data loads; asserts exact independently defined wire fields.

tests.name: filters by status and counts each filter
tests.reason: Status filters/counts must group stopped with success and interrupted with failure; verifies selected run IDs and data counts, not rendered row counts.

tests.name: merges the live page with older pages, the live copy winning, newest first
tests.reason: History merging must preserve one row per run with live/known state winning and chronological order; initial store list loads do not own older-page composition.

tests.name: shows the run asked for, else the newest live one, else the newest
tests.reason: Run navigation must keep an explicitly requested older run, otherwise select a live run before a completed one and handle an empty list. Detects jumping away from a notification target.

tests.name: drops a row with no id or name, and repairs the rest field by field
tests.reason: Malformed summary rows/fields must not enter typed client state or attach another workflow's run; fixtures independently specify valid vs invalid wire values.

tests.name: keeps the listed errors and what they leave out
tests.reason: Wire summary errors and omitted count must survive sanitization so a truncated list still communicates all blocking failures.

tests.name: an older daemon's row (the count alone) has no list
tests.reason: Mixed-version summary compatibility must retain error counts without fabricating detailed problems absent from the old daemon response.

tests.name: repairs a malformed list entry by entry, and never counts fewer errors than it lists
tests.reason: Malformed error arrays must retain valid blocking problems, drop warnings/invalid entries, and avoid contradictory counts; AGENTS demands payload validation.

tests.name: loads once, shares a request in flight, and refreshes when stale
tests.reason: Concurrent panel consumers share a load, loaded data stays cached, and stale refresh removes absent workflows; visible refresh convergence plus request lifecycle, not private collaborator ordering.

tests.name: a failure is the error state, and a refresh failure keeps the rows
tests.reason: Initial load error must surface, while refresh failure retains prior rows with stale/error state; prevents disappearing workflows during network outages.

tests.name: an event that crosses the answer is not undone by it
tests.reason: A list response crossing newer upsert/delete events must not regress names or resurrect deleted records; held response catches real network race.

tests.name: a client of another connection resets first
tests.reason: Loading another connection must replace prior daemon data rather than mix identically scoped workflows.

tests.name: ignores malformed payloads and unknown types without a throw
tests.reason: Malformed or unknown events must leave state intact and avoid throwing through event dispatch; valid event cases make this meaningful validation coverage.

tests.name: repeated events neither duplicate rows nor resurrect deleted workflows
tests.reason: Repeated upserts must preserve one record and cannot defeat deletion tombstones; detects reconnect event replay resurrecting removed workflows.

tests.name: a run's start, updates and end fold into its workflow's row
tests.reason: Run start/progress/end must update row/cache together and never revert terminal state due to late events or stale summaries; lower server tests do not protect UI convergence.

tests.name: a secrets change marks the scopes it touches stale
tests.reason: Workflow-scoped secret changes stale only that scope; global changes stale every inherited list and malformed scoped metadata is discarded.

tests.name: block updates accept a retry but ignore an earlier attempt or state
tests.reason: A retry's newer attempt may return to running while old attempts/earlier same-attempt states cannot regress progress; unique ordering invariant.

tests.name: a workflow's recent runs load newest first, and a started run joins them
tests.reason: Recent runs must be isolated by workflow, ordered newest first, and accept new started runs; pagination composition is a separate caller.

tests.name: a loaded run keeps the deltas that landed while it was in flight
tests.reason: A loaded detail response must retain newer block deltas received in flight while adding previously unknown blocks.

tests.name: a reconnect marks a held run stale; a forced reload clears it and takes the run's end
tests.reason: Reconnect must mark held detail stale and a successful forced fetch must learn its terminal status and clear staleness.

tests.name: a list refresh updates the summary of a run held whole
tests.reason: A history refresh must update an already loaded whole run's summary, recovering missed terminal events through a different response path.

tests.name: a run whose definition does not parse is not published and does not crash
tests.reason: Malformed frozen workflow definitions must be discarded before shared run state while load remains safe; catches invalid protocol data reaching run renderers.

tests.name: enabling shows at once, then carries the daemon's answer
tests.reason: Enable must show optimistic state, issue the current revision patch and adopt daemon-confirmed revision/state; daemon patch mocks do not implement UI overrides.

tests.name: a refusal rolls back and becomes the notice; a stale revision is re-read once
tests.reason: Stale enable requests must retry with fetched revision; rejected requests must roll back optimistic state and expose a dismissible error notice.

tests.name: an overlap skip offers Run anyway
tests.reason: An overlap skip must offer Run anyway and retry with force in the wire request, independently specified in §5.11.

tests.name: create shows the row at once; delete removes it, and a gone workflow counts as deleted
tests.reason: Successful create must immediately enter client state; delete of an already-gone server record still removes its client row.

tests.name: a write's own row lists the errors its answer carries
tests.reason: Write responses must update the workflow list with actual blocking errors, excluding warnings; list sanitization alone does not exercise write-result conversion.

tests.name: a reset drops answers still in flight
tests.reason: Reset during an in-flight response must discard the old answer and remain idle, preventing cross-connection stale data leakage.

tests.name: marks a project a known run names as its temp project
tests.reason: A known run temporary path must mark the corresponding project despite trailing slash normalization; avoids missing workflow attribution.

tests.name: never a deleted one, and never a wf- folder on its name alone
tests.reason: Deleted temp projects and merely similarly named user projects must not be attributed to a workflow; positive case prevents reject-all implementation.

tests.name: builds a last-day-of-month cron the scheduler accepts
tests.reason: Monthly last-day UI must serialize cron that runs Jan 31 and Feb 28 at selected time; independent calendar dates catch erroneous fixed-day schedules.

tests.name: accepts empty or valid JSON
tests.reason: Manual example input permits absence and valid JSON scalars/objects, so optional input must not block workflow editing.

tests.name: points at the line and column of a mistake
tests.reason: User JSON diagnostics must locate the actual malformed token in multiline input; asserted line/column are source positions, not arbitrary error prose.

tests.name: re-picking the current schedule kind changes nothing
tests.reason: Choosing the existing schedule kind must retain configured times, days and unknown fields; prevents silent resets while editing.

tests.name: switching the schedule kind starts it fresh, keeping the time of day
tests.reason: Schedule kind conversion must preserve selected time of day while producing a valid new preset; catches unexpected trigger firing time shifts.

tests.name: re-picking the current repository kind keeps the URL and account
tests.reason: Repository source edits must retain URL/credential/unknown fields when kind stays same and remove fields belonging to a different source kind.

tests.name: changing the account keeps every other repository field
tests.reason: Credential edits must preserve repository URL and future fields; clearing credentials must omit the account reference rather than send an invalid empty ID.

tests.name: re-picking the current event kind changes nothing
tests.reason: Git event kind re-selection must preserve filters and unknown fields; valid variant defaults avoid malformed trigger requests when switching.

tests.name: edits within an event keep its other fields
tests.reason: Editing one Git filter must preserve other event configuration and omit cleared optional filters; detects losing actions, future fields or broadened trigger matching.

tests.name: never sends an older build's credential: it prompts for a sign-in instead
tests.reason: An obsolete password-derived stored credential must be purged without making an authenticated info request, and the sign-in flow must appear. Detects legacy credential disclosure or unauthenticated fallback.

tests.name: a 401 drops the token, forgets it in memory and prompts once
tests.reason: A refused session token must leave storage and the in-memory client, and cause one sign-in prompt instead of a reconnect loop. Detects continued reuse of revoked credentials; error wording is incidental.

tests.name: an auth-info request that got no answer is retried, never taken for 'no sign-in needed'
tests.reason: An unreachable auth-info route must preserve the credential and reject to the connection retry loop without sending an uncredentialed request. Detects interpreting network failure as authentication being disabled.

tests.name: a daemon that answers without auth info (an older build's 404) still needs no sign-in
tests.reason: An older daemon with no auth-info route must continue through the compatibility path. Detects old-daemon lockout; this is a 404 route response, distinct from the network-error case.

tests.name: go with the credential when the daemon refuses it — that daemon's alone
tests.reason: A daemon refusing credentials must clear only its own persisted chat cache. Detects leaking cached private chats after revocation or deleting another daemon's cache.

tests.name: go when the remote is removed
tests.reason: Removing a remote must clear that daemon's persisted chats and preserve other daemon caches. Detects data remaining reachable after disconnecting the remote.

tests.name: go on sign-out
tests.reason: Signing out must remove that daemon's persisted chat cache. Detects private chat data remaining after logout; revocation/removal use different app actions.

tests.name: stores the returned token and the username, never the password
tests.reason: Login must send normalized username plus the entered password once, persist only returned token/username, then reconnect using that token. Detects password-at-rest or password-derived bearer regressions.

tests.name: a wrong password or a lockout keeps the prompt with its reason and stores nothing
tests.reason: 401 and Retry-After-bearing 429 login failures must retain the prompt, expose the refusal/retry duration and store no credentials. Detects accepting rejected login or silently bypassing rate-limit guidance.

tests.name: refuses a response that is not a token
tests.reason: A malformed login token must not be persisted or connected with, and must produce an error state. Detects trusting a legacy/password-equivalent response; exact generated wording is unnecessary.

tests.name: says so when the SSH key was refused and the clone went over HTTPS
tests.reason: A successful clone that fell back from SSH to HTTPS must relay the daemon's supplied notice. Detects silent transport fallback; only notice data matters, not the toast title.

tests.name: stays quiet for a clone over its first transport, and for a daemon that sends no report
tests.reason: An ordinary clone or older daemon omitting a fallback report must not manufacture a warning. Detects false fallback warnings for normal SSH/HTTPS cloning.

tests.name: created and updated upsert; closed removes and moves the active tab on
tests.reason: Create/update desktop events must upsert visible data; a close event removes the desktop and hands focus to another tab. Detects stale desktop tabs or lost updates.

tests.name: malformed payloads never reach state
tests.reason: Malformed desktop and window event payloads must leave state untouched. Detects unvalidated wire values crashing the desktop UI.

tests.name: desktop.windows patches that desktop's windows and active window
tests.reason: A windows event must patch the named desktop's window list/active id without changing another desktop. Detects cross-desktop window routing.

tests.name: closing a desktop dismisses its pending confirm and retargets an open launch dialog
tests.reason: A closed desktop must clear its pending close confirmation and retarget an open launch dialog. Detects subsequent launches or confirmations referencing a dead desktop.

tests.name: createDesktopWithApp posts, adds the desktop and activates its tab
tests.reason: Creating a desktop with an app must send the public request, hold its returned desktop and activate that project tab. Detects dropped launch data or an invisible successful launch.

tests.name: launchIntoDesktop posts the app, records it and focuses that desktop
tests.reason: Launching into an existing desktop must send the app request, attach the returned app and focus that desktop. Detects launches recorded under the wrong desktop.

tests.name: a daemon refusal rejects so the dialog can show it
tests.reason: A desktop creation refusal must reject with the API error and add no desktop. Detects a false successful/phantom launch.

tests.name: the launch dialog opens and closes
tests.reason: Opening and closing the launch dialog must publish/remove its target through actual app actions. This is the only action-level owner; deleting it would leave a broken menu-open action undetected.

tests.name: running apps always ask first, even with session confirms off
tests.reason: Closing a desktop with live apps must ask first even when terminal confirmation is disabled; confirmation invokes the close request. Detects terminating apps without consent.

tests.name: a desktop with no running apps closes without asking
tests.reason: A desktop whose apps exited must close without confirmation and remove its tab after the request. Detects an unnecessary blocked close flow.

tests.name: a failed stop keeps the tab and says why; an already-gone desktop is dropped
tests.reason: A refused close must preserve its tab and relay the supplied error; an already-missing desktop must be removed. Detects hiding a live failed-to-stop desktop or leaving an unrecoverable stale tab.

tests.name: opens a Files tab on the file when the project has none
tests.reason: Revealing a file must create and activate a project Files tab when none exists. Detects changed-file links doing nothing.

tests.name: reuses the first Files tab and bumps the nonce, even for the same file
tests.reason: Repeated reveal must reuse the existing Files tab and change the reveal notification even for the same path, without changing other tabs. Detects duplicate tabs or ignored repeated navigation.

tests.name: carries a line and column to jump to (a terminal's file:line:col link)
tests.reason: File-link line and column must reach the reveal target and be cleared by a later plain file reveal. Detects lost terminal-link location or a stale jump.

tests.name: does nothing without a current project
tests.reason: Reveal outside a project must create no project-local tab. Detects orphaned tabs associated with no active project.

tests.name: re-sends the same commandId after an unknown outcome, and a fresh one once it answered
tests.reason: An unknown fork outcome from host unavailability or network loss must retry the same commandId; an answered fork frees that id. Detects duplicated chats after reconnect, through actual app/API calls.

tests.name: a refusal frees the point, and another fork point never reuses the id
tests.reason: A definite refusal must free the command id and a different fork point must use another id. Detects unrelated forks being collapsed into a previous idempotent command.

tests.name: closing the stray fork tab (or the daemon taking it back) frees the kept id
tests.reason: Closing a stray fork through session events or the app action must free the retained retry id. Detects subsequent forks returning a closed tab or COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT; pure point-isolation cases remain in lineage.logic.test.ts.

tests.name: an older listing answering last does not overwrite the newer one
tests.reason: A late older project listing must not overwrite the newer listing, including repo identity fields. Detects a clone disappearing from its repository group.

tests.name: stays loading until the newest call settles, whatever the older one does
tests.reason: An older failed listing must not clear loading while the newest listing is pending. Detects premature empty-state rendering under concurrent refreshes.

tests.name: a listing that lands after the workspace closed is dropped
tests.reason: A listing completing after the workspace closes must not repopulate project state. Detects showing projects from a closed workspace.

tests.name: shows the opening screen until the tab exists, and ignores a second click meanwhile
tests.reason: Resume must expose its in-flight opening state, suppress double-click launch and activate the returned tab. Detects duplicate sessions or a never-ending opening view.

tests.name: clears the opening screen when the launch fails
tests.reason: A failed resumed launch must clear the opening state and propagate the actual error. Detects a permanently blocked composer after launch failure.

tests.name: switches to the tab that already holds the conversation instead of failing
tests.reason: CONVERSATION_ALREADY_OPEN with a local owner must activate that tab and clear resume error. Detects refusing a conversation already available in the project.

tests.name: still refuses when the owning tab is not in this project
tests.reason: An already-open owner absent from this project must preserve the daemon's refusal instead of activating a foreign tab. Detects cross-project activation.

tests.name: a new chat and a resumed conversation launch with the agent's remembered profile
tests.reason: New and resumed agent chats must carry the agent's remembered profile while resume identity remains intact. Detects silent profile omission or broken resume.

tests.name: Global (nothing remembered, or another agent's pick) sends no profile
tests.reason: Global and another agent's remembered pick must omit profileId from the launch; explicitly picking Global clears the preference. Detects loading another agent's profile.

tests.name: a deleted profile is no agent's pick any more
tests.reason: A deleted-profile event must remove remembered picks of that profile. Detects the next launch being stuck on a deleted kit.

tests.name: a remembered profile the daemon no longer has: the pick is forgotten and the notice says so — nothing launches as Global
tests.reason: A missing remembered profile must clear its preference, explain failure and open no replacement Global session. Detects silent fallback to different instructions.

tests.name: a remembered profile that is not ready keeps the pick and says why and how to pick another
tests.reason: A not-ready remembered profile must keep its preference and relay the preparation failure. Detects silently changing the kit or swallowing the supplied diagnostic; generic help wording is incidental.
tests.currentName: a remembered profile that is not ready keeps the pick and reports the failure

tests.name: another refusal of a launch that named its own profile still throws
tests.reason: An explicitly requested missing profile must propagate its refusal instead of applying remembered-profile recovery. Detects incorrectly clearing or overriding a caller's explicit choice.

tests.name: the daemon's profile list prunes remembered picks it does not have (an unreadable one is kept)
tests.reason: A loaded profile list must prune missing remembered picks but preserve an unreadable profile reported separately. Detects discarding a recoverable kit or retaining deleted picks.

tests.name: picks are kept per daemon connection
tests.reason: Profile preferences must persist under the active daemon connection key. Detects one daemon's choice overwriting another daemon's preference.

tests.name: a terminal launch never carries one
tests.reason: Terminal launches must omit Agent Profiles even if the refId has a stored preference. Detects chat-only context leaking into shell requests.

tests.name: arrive with a session update and are cleared by the next one's empty list
tests.reason: Session updates must carry pending merge requests and an explicit empty list must clear them. Detects stale merge-back action buttons after the final request completes.

tests.name: a change replaces the whole list
tests.reason: A plugins change event must replace the whole list, including changed enable/job state. Detects stale plugin status after another client changes it.

tests.name: malformed payloads and other event types never reach state
tests.reason: Malformed plugin payloads and unrelated event types must not change state. Detects unvalidated plugin wire values reaching typed UI state.

tests.name: stores the daemon's list
tests.reason: A plugin-list request must publish the daemon's actual list. Detects the initial connect hiding enabled plugins until a later event.

tests.name: rejects with the request's error and keeps the last list
tests.reason: A failed plugin refresh must reject with its cause and retain the previous list. Detects presenting failed refresh as success or losing visible plugin state.

tests.name: drops an answer that lands after a connection switch
tests.reason: A plugin-list answer from a previous daemon client must be discarded. Detects cross-connection plugin state leakage.

tests.name: applies one plugin's state from a route's answer
tests.reason: Duplicate of lib/plugins-state.test.ts insert/replace/null-list coverage: the app action only forwards to upsertPluginIn and this case adds no independent route or event wiring. Fails unique-protection bar 6.

tests.name: reloads the workspace's projects once when it exits or closes
tests.reason: A typed-clone setup terminal exiting must refresh its workspace exactly once, and unrelated exits must not refresh it. Detects a completed clone staying ungrouped or duplicate refresh effects.

tests.name: closing the tab of a running setup also reloads
tests.reason: Closing a running setup tab must refresh the new project listing even without an exit event. Detects missing clone state after user close.

tests.name: leaves the list alone when another workspace is open by then
tests.reason: A setup exit while another workspace is selected must not replace that workspace's projects. Detects cross-workspace state contamination.

tests.name: follows the project's git status: a landed clone reloads until it shows its repo
tests.reason: Git-status events must refresh until the clone has a repo identity, then unsubscribe and ignore a later exit. Detects missing repository grouping or endless refresh after completion.

tests.name: a clone that lands before the terminal is open still reloads
tests.reason: A clone-status event arriving before the setup tab resolves must be remembered and applied after creation. Detects fast clones whose only event is lost.

tests.name: stops following when the terminal exits, and when it never opened
tests.reason: Following must stop after setup close and after a setup tab never opens. Detects leaked event streams and background refresh after launch failure.

tests.name: while another workspace is open, asks the daemon without touching the store's list
tests.reason: While another workspace is open, clone refresh must read its original workspace without mutating the visible project list. Detects cross-workspace list replacement.

tests.name: a template setup is not followed
tests.reason: Template setup commands must not acquire clone-follow subscriptions or reload on exit. Detects unbounded monitoring of repos with no clone identity.

tests.name: a connection switch stops every follow
tests.reason: A daemon connection switch must stop all clone follows; late git/exit events must no longer refresh. Detects old-connection side effects after navigation.

tests.name: opens a tab per file, titled by the file name, and focuses an open one again
tests.reason: Whiteboards must open once per file in a project, use that file's name and reactivate an existing tab. Detects duplicate editor instances for the same drawing.

tests.name: closing the active whiteboard tab activates another tab of the project
tests.reason: Closing an active whiteboard must activate another tab in its project. Detects an empty main view while another drawing is open.

tests.name: does nothing outside a project
tests.reason: Opening a whiteboard without a project must create no tab. Detects unscoped file-editor state.

tests.name: writes an empty scene to whiteboards/Untitled.excalidraw and opens it
tests.reason: New whiteboard creation must upload to whiteboards/Untitled.excalidraw with a non-overwriting conflict policy before opening the returned file. Detects opening an unsaved drawing or overwriting another drawing.

tests.name: takes a numbered name when Untitled is taken
tests.reason: An existing Untitled drawing must retry using rename and open the daemon's numbered filename. Detects replacing the existing drawing or losing the successful retry.

tests.name: raises a notice and opens nothing when the file cannot be written
tests.reason: Folder conflict must open no drawing and report an error; an explicitly injected upload failure must preserve its supplied cause in the notice. Detects phantom tabs or silent failed writes, independent of generated copy.
